sense.text:
“But we are bound to give thanks alway to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord.” Read it slowly. Which one of us gives thanks to God every day for the brother sitting next to us, for the sister sitting next to us? Ask yourself that question, because that is what this verse is saying.

That is the spirit we have to war with from now on: not to have an evil thought of a brother or an evil thought of a sister. It is time to stop following Satan, and to pray for the brothers and fast for the brothers, so that we may be found faithful in the eyes of God.

“Because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation.” It is no coincidence that we are in here. The salvation we are receiving was given to us from the beginning. Many think it is a coincidence they are here, and that is why they are wasting time and doing nothing with their life. You are here because you were chosen from the beginning.

precepts.why:
How do we know it is no coincidence? John shows it: “They went out from us, but they were not of us.” There are going to be brothers and sisters who come among us, but they were not of us.

“For if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us.” No matter what we went through, they would still be with us. In this body we are going to go through things; if this is the hospital, we all need medicine, and the word of God is what is going to heal us. A sister said she left because a sister offended her. How many times do we offend the Lord? We have to build our spirit up, not move through every little stupidity.

“But they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.” They were not the chosen. So you that are here, it is not a coincidence: you were chosen from the beginning.

Deacon Malachiyah drew the same out for a marriage. Some brothers learn that they are the children of Israel, and the wife gets up and leaves: I don’t want to be with you no more. A spouse who truly loved you, even not believing what you believe, would be pleased to dwell with you: I can’t see my life without you, so I will do what you tell me in the scriptures because I love you. If that spouse gets up and leaves because of the truth, that person never really loved you, brothers, and the same for you sisters. To hell with them. The Most High is giving you a blessing.

sense.text:
The topic is a tree bearing no fruits, and it begins here. “Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest the fruit of thy seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of thy vineyard, be defiled.” If you sow the vineyard with different kinds of seed, the fruit is going to be defiled.

Reading that, we might think it is only about agriculture or farming, but it is talking about much more than that. When we go and deal with other nations, the kids that are brought forth, the descendants, are defiled. They are confused. So this law is not just talking about agriculture.

precepts.why:
Ecclesiasticus explains how the vineyard is defiled. “My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.” The strangers are the heathens, the other nations, and he goes on to show how you give your strength to them.

“When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed.” A fruitful possession: you got a position, you got money, you are rich. Sow it with your own seed means sow it with your own people. Don’t be going and marrying no damn white woman. That is how you keep your strength. Today a lot of brothers get money, and the first thing they do is go marry a heathen; when you marry the heathens when you are rich, you are giving your strength unto strangers. Deal with your own people: start a family with the woman God created for you.

“Trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” Your stock is your nationality, your race, your people. You being a son of God, why would you go deal with other nations? “So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified”: when you have riches and marry your sisters and bring forth children among your own people, your children and your race are magnified.

“Having the confidence of their good descent.” The good descent means you are not confused about what your nationality is, because you were not sowing your seed among all kinds of heathens, as our forefathers were doing in the book of Nehemiah. That is why Deuteronomy says the fruit of a vineyard sown with divers seeds is defiled.

sense.text:
Malcolm X explained how the Nation of Islam grew: men had preached on the street corners of Harlem for some thirty years and nobody listened, then within ten years the people were listening by the millions. A seed stays beneath the soil until the season changes, and God brought about political, social and economic conditions that made the minds of our people fertile to the seed. The Nation of Islam is idolatry, and it is not the way to go; it is only an analogy. Those conditions are oppression. The seed only grows when the season is right, and God’s seed grows under oppression.

For years we have been on the street teaching, by the foolishness of preaching, but we have not yet seen the abundance of the trees and fruits from the seeds that were planted. Now Trump went into office, the world changed, oppression has risen up on our people, the KKK and Nazis march cursing all black people, telling them to go back to their country. Because of all these things, our people’s minds are becoming receptive and fertile.

In the forties and fifties the Nation of Islam rose up while our people were oppressed; the Black Panther Party rose up to fight against it; Martin Luther King, Marcus Garvey, the Young Lords and AIM, many leaders and movements rose up. But “God hath set forth us the apostles last.” All those movements rose up, it has been over eighty years, and it did not profit us: they killed Malcolm X and nobody hears of the Nation of Islam any more. We have been Muslims, Christians and Black Panthers, and our people are in the same condition. So the Most High sent the 144 last. God has sent thousands of men on the earth in these last days, and we are planting the seed of God in the hearts of our people.

“As it were appointed to death.” The twelve apostles are here today in the last days, and they will die doing this work. The same way Marcus Garvey and Malcolm X were killed, these men will be killed too: teaching, planting seed, waking the people up and standing up for our people who are being oppressed today.

Everything Malcolm said in that video is shown here in Isaiah 30: the right condition and season had to come for the seed to grow, and that condition is affliction.

“And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity”: that is what our people are going through today. Turn on YouTube or the news and all you see is rioting and adversity. “And the water of affliction”: our people are crying tears, their kids are being taken away from them and put in detention centers.

“Yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more.” The teachers are the husbandmen, the planters, the brothers planting the seed. Affliction is the right environment, the season to plant, when our people are looking for answers to why these things are happening. We have been Muslims and Christians and nothing changed. So God says, I am going to afflict you, and while I am afflicting you I am going to send teachers to teach you why you are being afflicted and to plant my word, my seed, in you. This climate of affliction we are living in right now is the best time for us to go and plant the seed of the word of God.

“But thine eyes shall see thy teachers”: the people have to see us. They will see us on the street corner teaching the word of God.

“And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it.” The way is: repent, you are an Israelite, Christ is a black man, come out from her my people. The people will be hearing these things. Repent and come back to your nationality.

“When ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left”: whichever way they turn they are going to be seeing us. They can’t run from the word of God.

“Ye shall defile also the covering of thy graven images of silver, and the ornament of thy molten images of gold.” That means they will repent. A lot of our people are going to repent under that season of affliction.

“Thou shalt cast them away as a menstruous cloth; thou shalt say unto it, Get thee hence.” You are going to cast away Christianity. You are going to cast away being a Muslim.

“Then shall he give the rain of thy seed.” It is speaking of planting, and the right season to plant is in affliction. Then God gives rain to the seed, and the seed is the word of God that is planted in all of us.

“That thou shalt sow the ground withal”: to sow the ground is planting, waking Israel up. We plant the seeds, and the Lord sends rain to water them. “And bread of the increase of the earth, and it shall be fat and plenteous”: the increase is Israel growing and multiplying. This is the beginning stages, brothers, and it shall be plenteous.

“For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater.” Rain and snow come from heaven and do not return; go outside and you see the snow all over the place, not melting. They come down and water the earth so that it brings forth.

That rain coming down from heaven is the word of God, and the seed is God’s word dwelling in all of us.

“So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void.” When God’s word comes on the earth, people change, people repent. It does its job on the earth right now. Look at us: God’s word came, and we heard it. That is why we are all here, because at one point we heard the word of God. When you teach and plant that seed, God’s word does not go out void.

“It shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it.” What did God send his word to do? To wake us up. He sent his word, which is the seed, to wake us up.

“All the trees of the field shall clap their hands.” The trees of the field are us: that seed has turned into a tree.

“Instead of the thorn shall come up the fir tree, and instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle tree.” The thorns are wickedness, sin and evil, the wicked brothers and sisters, and the brier is the wicked too. In their place come up fir trees and myrtle trees.

The Most High called his word a seed; the seed grew and turned into a tree. “And it shall be to the Lord for a name, for an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off.” That tree is not going to be cut off.

“Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord, and whose hope the Lord is. For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters.” If you trust in the Lord, brothers and sisters, you will be that tree planted by the water. Before that tree grew it was a seed, and that seed is the word of God.

“That spreadeth out her roots by the river”: the river is water, and all trees need water in order to grow and become strong. “And shall not see when heat cometh”: you are not going to see it when heat or drought comes, because you are by the water, and the water is the word of God.

“But her leaf shall be green”: your leaves will be green, not dry and withered. The dry and withering leaves are the brothers and sisters who don’t study, who are falling off and going off.

“Neither shall cease from yielding fruit.” The fruits we are supposed to be yielding are the fruits of the spirit: love, joy, peace, brotherly kindness, patience. When the seed is planted a tree grows, and the tree is supposed to bear fruit. All of us are supposed to bring forth fruits once the word of God is in us.

“For as the husbandman soweth much seed upon the ground, and planteth many trees.” The husbandman is the Most High God, and the much seed is us.

“And yet the thing that is sown good in his season.” Every seed cannot be sown in the same season, as Malcolm showed: there is a certain time to plant certain crops, and some crops you cannot plant in the winter, the summer or the spring. Some seeds only grow in harsh conditions, and that harsh season is affliction.

“Cometh not up, neither doth all that is planted take root.” Anyone who has planted, in the islands or anywhere, knows that some seeds grow and take root and some do not. So it is with us: the seed, the word of God, is in some of you, but you are not going to take root in this truth. You heard the word of God and you are here, but you are not going to grow and turn into a tree.

“Even so is it of them that are sown in the world; they shall not all be saved.” That is us being sown in the world. All of us in whom God has sown his word are not going to be saved, because some will not do what is right, will stay in their sin, will not change and will not bring forth fruits. Everybody who comes through these doors is not going to be saved: he that endureth to the end shall be saved.

“Like as the husbandman’s seed perisheth, if it come not up.” The word God sows in you can perish. If it does not come up, it never takes root, or thorns grow around it.

“And receive not thy rain in due season.” The rain is the word, wisdom, and it has to come in due season.

“Or if there come too much rain, and corrupt it.” Those who plant know that if too much rain falls on a seed, the seed does not grow. It is the same with the word of God: too much rain is too much wisdom, getting too much and not being able to handle it. The brothers and sisters like it when the teaching goes heavy, but too much of that wisdom could corrupt them, so the teaching has to ease up off of that. Too much rain corrupts someone because they become high-minded and puffed up, and fall into the condemnation of the devil.
“Even so perisheth man also, which is formed with thy hands, and is called thine own image.” “And likened him unto the husbandman’s seed.” We are the husbandman’s seed.

precepts.why:
How can too much rain corrupt a seed? “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.” A novice is somebody new in this truth, a beginner. Some have been here two years, some five years, and some brothers catch on real quick.

Why would a novice get lifted up with pride? Because he got too much rain, too much wisdom, and he starts getting high-minded. Then he falls into the condemnation of the devil: Satan destroys that seed that is in him. That is what it means when the scripture says too much rain can corrupt the seed. As it is said, knowledge puffs up, but charity edifies.

The deacons have been learning for over twenty years. When they go into certain things, it comes from years of being watered, not from waking up one day able to break down scriptures.

sense.text:
This goes into the rain. “For he hath given you the former rain moderately.” Moderately, because too much rain corrupts the seed. The waters come to the ankles, then to the knees, and they keep rising: that is how the Most High operates. He raises the water moderately so we can handle it, and that is why, as time goes on, the Most High shows us different levels in what we read in the scriptures.

“The former rain, and the latter rain”: there is rain in different seasons.

“And the floors shall be full of wheat, and the fats shall overflow with wine and oil.” This is talking about a harvest, but it is also talking about us. God will restore the years that the locust has eaten, and “ye shall eat in plenty, and be satisfied, and praise the name of the Lord your God.” He gives us the former rain and the latter rain and everything becomes bountiful. You might read it and think it is just farming. It is not just farming.

“And my people shall never be ashamed.” God says his people shall never be ashamed.

“And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else.” When this happens we are going to know that God is in the midst of Israel, and that there is no other God but our God.

“And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.” This explains what the rain is: it is God’s spirit. The spirit of Christ is going to be poured upon us.

“And your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions”: we are going to prophesy. “And also upon the servants and upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out my spirit.” The spirit God pours out on us is the rain.

Christ gives a parable. “A sower went out to sow his seed”: the seed is the word of God, and it is an example of the word of God being sown on the earth, in us.

“Some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.” Here comes Satan and takes away the word that was planted in him.

“And some fell upon a rock; and as soon as it was sprung up, it withered away.” That is some in this truth: you come, you hear the word and you start growing, a year, two years, three, four, and then you just wither away. We don’t see you no more. You just disappear.

“Because it lacked moisture.” The moisture is the water. What is important for the seed to grow into a tree is water, the word of God.

“And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.” As the seed is growing, thorns spring up with it, like the weeds that grow with a plant in a garden. The thorns are sin: the cares of this world, the lusts of the flesh and the sins we all deal with. As God’s word grows in you, the thorns are there too; Paul had a thorn in the flesh. You have to weed out and cut down those thorns, or they will wrap around and choke the word of God in you and destroy you, and you become unfruitful.

“And other fell on good ground, and sprang up, and bare fruit an hundredfold.” Some brothers and sisters will fall on good ground and grow in this truth and bear fruit a hundredfold, and that fruit is the fruits of the spirit.

The seed on the rock withered because it had no moisture. Here is how the seed gets its water. “Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed”: they were ministers, planters, farmers.

“I have planted, Apollos watered.” Paul planted the seed: he woke the brothers and sisters up, taught them about Christ and to repent. Apollos came and watered it: he taught them, pouring the water on the seed that was planted. The one pouring the water is the one teaching you, just as the teachers are watering you right now. Apollos could not pour too much water, or the seed would corrupt and not take root; so the teaching draws back from going heavy, though from time to time it has to go heavy.

There is a skill to it. Paul had a skill of planting and Apollos a skill of watering; if he does not have it, he puts too much water on the plant and messes it up. Not every seed grows the same way. Some seeds can only be planted on certain moons, some plants take a lot of water and some cannot; a farmer understands these things. Wisdom raineth down skill, and Paul called himself a wise master builder, because it is not a simple thing to build men, or even to water.

“But God gave the increase.” The increase is the fruits coming forth from the tree. The teachers in IUIC water you, go over the law with you, how to fight this and overcome that. It is up to you to take this truth seriously, go home and study, cut out the thorns growing in you and bear root. To bear root is to believe this truth for yourself: not here because of your friend or some brother, but because you believe what the Bible says, trust in the Lord, and study the scriptures at home. Then God gives you the increase. That is the only way you are going to grow as a tree.

“So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase.” It is God that does the whole thing, so you cannot be high-minded in this truth, thinking it is you doing it. The brother who taught you that you are Israel did his job, and the one watering you does his, but both are nothing: the Most High could replace either one.

“Now he that planteth and he that watereth are one: and every man shall receive his own reward.” Every one of us is going to receive our own reward: the brother on the street planting the seed and the brother watering the seed.

“He hungered. And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only.” Christ found no fruits on the fig tree, only leaves. The trees represent us.

“Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.” He was hungry, he could do nothing with that tree, so he told it no fruit would ever grow on it again, and the tree withered and died. Christ literally went to a tree looking for fruit, but it is an analogy: that tree represents each one of us. If the word of God is planted in you and you are growing in this truth, what is the sense of being an olive tree and bearing no olives? What is the sense of being a tree and bearing no fruits? You are good for nothing.
Christ also spoke a parable on it. “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.”

“Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard.” The dresser of the vineyard is the teacher, the one watering the tree.

“Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none.” Three years this brother or sister has been in the body, and there are no fruits of the spirit. The same person you were three years ago when you heard the word of God is the same person you are today. Charity didn’t pop up. You bear no fruits.

“Cut it down.” If we are in this truth and not bearing the fruits of the spirit, the Lord is going to get rid of us, all of us. “Why cumbereth it the ground?” That tree is good for nothing. Why are you here among us just taking up space, if you are not trying to change?

“Lord, let it alone this year also.” This is Christ speaking on our behalf. “Till I shall dig about it, and dung it.” To dig around it is so it can be irrigated and the water can flow through; to dung it is to put fertilizer, nutrients, around the tree so it can bring forth fruit. That is the teachers: all of you are being dug around and dunged right now with the word of God. We are making the soil nice so the water can irrigate through it. Whether you bring forth fruit is on you.

“And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.” You don’t know how long the Lord is going to be patient with you. If you are in this truth and not bearing fruits, not becoming a better person, not learning, not rooted, the Lord could be saying right now: next year I’m getting rid of this dude, next month I’m getting rid of this sister. It is serious like that.

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love”: the love is you keeping the commandments. These are the fruits you are supposed to bring forth, the fruits the Lord wants to see inside of us.

“Joy”: do you have joy in keeping God’s commandments, or are you always damn sad and depressed? Some are always depressed: stay away from me. You don’t got the fruit of the spirit. “Peace”: peace with your wife, peace with the brothers and sisters. Always arguing and fighting with each other is not the fruit of the spirit.

“Longsuffering” is being patient. “Gentleness” is being kind and gentle, right with your brother; it does not mean being soft or acting like a sodomite. “Faith”: you must believe what the Bible says; that is one of the fruits.

“Meekness”: you are humble. “Temperance” is self-control: people don’t just get you angry, you are not easily provoked. These are the fruits you develop once the word of God is dwelling in you.

“Against such there is no law.” Why? Because you are keeping the law.

Here are the fruits of the spirit also. “And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge.” You must have virtue. You must have knowledge: learning the scriptures, learning how to break them down. We are not going to be on social media all the time, so you have to learn the knowledge of God. Brothers among us who are not coming around the deacons, the bishops and the officers to learn the knowledge of God are not going to last in this truth.

“And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness”: you must learn patience and learn to be godly. “And to godliness brotherly kindness”: we must be brotherly and kind to each other. “And to brotherly kindness charity”: love God with all your heart and love your brother as yourself. All of these are the fruits your tree must be bringing forth.

“For if these things be in you, and abound.” To abound means they stay in you. These things can be in you and then leave you: you can be bearing fruits and stop. Some are among us six or seven years, growing and developing fruits, leaves green, and then somebody offends them and they stop bringing forth fruits; all these things leave them.

“They make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” For you not to be barren and unfruitful, these things have to be in you and stay in you. We do not change up.

“But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.” If you lack these things you are blind, and you have forgotten that you were purged from your old sins. You have to have these things inside of you for your tree to bring forth the fruits of the spirit.

“For wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction.” That is all the things out in the world; it is broad, and many things can destroy you in this world. “And many there be which go in thereat”: many people get caught up in a lot of evil.

“Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life.” That narrow way is the commandments of God. If you want life, the kingdom, you have to walk that narrow path by keeping the commandments.

“And few there be that find it.” That goes back to many are called, few are chosen, and to not everyone in whom the seed is sown being saved.

“Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. Ye shall know them by their fruits.” The fruits they bring forth from their spirit. If they don’t have charity, brotherly kindness, love, keeping the commandments, joy, they don’t have the fruit of the spirit. If they have envy, emulation, hatred, adultery and fornication, those are the fruits of the flesh. A false prophet is going to be doing evil things; that is how we will know if somebody is not right.

“Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.” Brothers and sisters, you want to bring forth good fruits. When you see brothers and sisters keep doing evil and not repent of it, that tree is corrupt. “A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.”

“Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.” If you are not bringing forth the fruits of the spirit, the Lord is going to cut you down and cast you into the fire, and that is damnation. If you are among us, examine yourself: am I bringing forth good fruits or evil fruits?

“Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.” That is why some are not to be dealt with: they are bringing forth evil fruits and not repenting, so be very mindful.

“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven.” There will be a lot of brothers and sisters who learn this gospel, but not because you say Lord, Lord are you going to enter the kingdom of heaven.
“I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.” Christ is the true vine and his Father is the husbandman, the same husbandman whose seed we read of in Ezra.

“Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” The Father is going to take it away, and the fruits are the fruits of the spirit.

“And every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.” To purge is to prune the tree. If you grow tomatoes, to get a lot of fruit you have to get rid of the dead branches and the extra leaves hanging below, because all that extra takes away the nutrients; pruned, the tree gets more water and more nutrients from the earth and brings forth more fruit.

How does he purge us? He puts us through trials and tribulations. When bad things happen to you, or correction comes, if you are righteous you understand that you are being purged, because the Lord needs you to bring forth more fruit. If you are bringing forth fruits, the Lord wants more, so he prunes the tree and puts you through things to make you better.

“Abide in me, and I in you.” Christ literally abides in us. Every last one of us who has the word of God sown in us, his spirit is in us.

“As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.” You cannot become better or grow fruits by yourself; Christ has to be in you. If you are not bearing fruits, not changing, not becoming a better person, maybe the Lord’s spirit is not dwelling in you. You must abide in Christ in order to bear fruit.

“I am the vine, ye are the branches.” Christ is the vine and we are the branches. “He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit”: if you believe in Christ and keep the commandments, you are abiding in Christ, his spirit is dwelling in you, and you bring forth much fruit.

“For without me ye can do nothing.” Without Christ dwelling in us we can’t overcome anything or do anything in this truth. That is why we always give the Lord the glory. Even the teaching given now is the Lord speaking through his servants, not glory for ourselves, and the growth of IUIC and the things we are doing on this earth are the Lord working through us and using us.

“If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered.” The brothers and sisters you see walk out of here, why do they leave? Because Christ is not dwelling in them; Christ was never in them. If he were dwelling in them, they would not wither away. Now they are back in Christianity talking about why I left: they made me keep the Sabbath.

The fruits of the spirit are not only within yourself; they are shared. Christ gave the two greatest commandments, love God with all your heart and love your neighbour, and that is how you know you have the fruit of the spirit: whatever you are going through, you learn to keep the unity of the brothers and the sisters. Running at any trouble like a damn dog, like a cat, and going back to Christianity shows you don’t know what the fruit of the spirit is. A lion doesn’t run, and neither does a wolf: we conquer.

“And men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.” They will be cast into the fire when Christ returns. That is literally what is done with dead branches that wither: they are burned as firewood. If there are no fruits in you and you wither away, God is going to use you for that.

“If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you.” That is the power we have once the spirit of Christ is dwelling in us: when we pray, the Lord answers our prayers.

“Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit.” The Lord wants us to bear much fruit, much fruit of the spirit; that is how God is glorified. “So shall ye be my disciples.” In order to be Christ’s disciples, brothers and sisters, we have to bear much fruit.

These are the last days, and it is getting worse and worse. This is the time to get ourselves right, get our spirit right and bring forth the fruits of the spirit, so the Lord does not cut you down, rather than going back to the world as a Muslim or talking about a white Jesus.
